GAP-ATTRIBUTION-001.precise_reason: The Yajurvedic third cannot be derived from anything held. data/staging/attribution/proofs/yv_katyayana_measurement.json measures the Madhyandina Sarvanukramani at NOT_EXTRACTABLE_AT_SOURCE_EXPLICIT: zero numeric mantra coordinates in 49,708 characters, 102 lingokta deferrals where the sutra declines to name the deity, and no field delimiters separating the rsi, devata and chandas slots. The one lead is an UNCHECKED printed edition (Weber 1852, or Uvata+Mahidhara) that may head each mantra with rsih/devata/chandah -- a page-image inspection, not a fetch. Until that source is acquired, YV devata dedication is unavailable at any evidence grade this graph accepts, so the three-Veda closure test cannot pass. The AV third is implementation-complete and lands. The SV third is implementation-complete and WITHHELD BY RULING, because a text-reuse edge is not a Samavedic ascription. So the gap is blocked on sources at both ends it could not reach, and is not unfinished implementation at either.

reasons_in_order_of_weight: 1. It is not a source attribution at all. DERIVED_FROM_A_COMPARISON_GRADE_EDGE is the field's own admission: the evidence is that an RV mantra's text recurs, not that any Samavedic authority ascribes a deity. The Samaveda is a liturgical rearrangement with its own ascriptive tradition, and projecting the Rigvedic dedication onto 1,662 of its 1,844 mantras would put attributions in the graph that no source states.

2. Owner decision 11 is directly on point: a fold may establish NORMALIZED_SURFACE_MATCH and may not be read as SAME_CANONICAL_PASSAGE. 504 of the 1,685 rest on the looser tiers -- SANDHI_INSENSITIVE 415, SCRIPT_FOLDED 89 -- and projecting a dedication across them is nearer a same-passage claim than a surface-match one.

3. Consistency across the sprint: 8 assertions were withheld from Agent 3 for resting on NEAR_PARALLEL_OF rather than exact, and Agent 7 refused a translation row whose 1.0 identity held on only 2 of 6 pairings -- 'a best-of-six identity is not identity'. What was refused over 8 assertions and 1 verse is not accepted over 1,662 verses.
sv_withheld_ruling.recorded_here_because: A decision that lives only in a transcript is a decision the next reader re-makes. It travels with the rows it governs, in sv_derived_dedications.jsonl and in proposed_mutations.json.

Every row keeps its source mantra, reuse tier, match_level and lcs_ratio, so a future Samavedic ascriptive source is checked AGAINST it rather than having to rebuild it.

GAP-COMMUNITIES-002.precise_reason: The GROUP half is closable now: all 33 carry a typed reason and it is staged. The PAIR half is not, and deliberately not, for two independent reasons. First, data/registry/devata_components.yaml states its own policy -- HAS_COMPONENT is human-reviewed enrichment and is NEVER inferred, not from a dual ending, not from a hyphen, not from a substring that looks like another entity's name -- so 24 dvandva decompositions inferred by an agent from a dual ending would violate that policy in exactly its own words. Second, the layer that would carry them stamps provenance_class = HUMAN_REVIEWED by default AND by validator (src/vedagraph/models/lexical.py:301,311) while no reviewer identity is recorded anywhere, and the shipped API tells every client that no edge in the graph is human-reviewed. Landing the PAIR half through that layer would create the first edges in the graph asserting a review nobody performed and make the API caveat false on the same day. The 24 rows are staged as an input to review, not as a substitute for it.
GAP-COMMUNITIES-002.prerequisite_before_the_pair_half_can_la: LexicalProvenanceClass needs a value that describes what this actually is -- CURATED_REGISTRY -- or ComponentAssertion needs to require a recorded reviewer identity, and data/registry/devata_components.yaml needs to carry one.
